summary: Tested the fix to POST /api/contabilita/rigenera (Prima nota 'Registra documenti mancanti'), which now also registers passive invoices still marked 'da_registrare'. I set up a TEST_T89 company with the contabilita module and aliquota_rc set to 10, then created: F, registered by hand (protocollo 1); A, a normal invoice; B, with a 200 EUR ritenuta; C, reverse charge with natura N6.3; P, dated last year; D, marked contestata; E, dated in a year closed via coge_chiusi. I also added one delivered (consegnata) sales invoice with its entry removed and one reconciled bank transaction. 9/9 pytest tests pass and passed again on a second full run. Results: A/B/C/P become 'registrata' with registrata_auto=true; data_registrazione equals the invoice date; protocolli are 2,3,4, continuing after the manual 1, with P getting 1 in its own year; C gets reverse_charge N6.3 at 10% with imposta 100. The accounting entries were regenerated with the invoice date (B: ritenute 200 avere / fornitori 1020 avere; C: iva_vendite 100 avere / iva_acquisti 100 dare). The response was acquisti=4, vendite=1, banca=1, and errori lists the closed-year invoice. D (contestata) and F are unchanged; E stays da_registrare. /passive?stato=da_registrare then holds only E, and the dashboard passive_da_registrare is 1, which is only E (closed year). Registro IVA acquisti lists F,A,B,C for this year and P for last year, and the RC row shows 10%/100. A second run returns 0/0/0 and creates no duplicate entries or protocolli. After reopening the closed year, E is registered with protocollo 1 in its year. UI: on /contabilita/prima-nota, coge-rigenera-btn shows the Italian confirm, then the toasts 'Registrate 1 vendite, 4 acquisti, 1 movimenti bancari' and the closed-year error, and the giornale reloads with the entries.

minor.issue: Regenerated purchase entries get new giornale numbers (9,10,11/2026) while keeping earlier dates. Entries created at import keep 1..7 with later dates, so the libro giornale numbering is no longer in date order.
If the invoice date is after today, data_registrazione is capped at today and ends up earlier than the invoice date. The manual PATCH rejects this case (dr < data). Edge case, not tested via API.
Contestata invoices still have (or get) an 'acquisto' accounting entry. In the test, contestata invoice D kept its FA entry in the prima nota. Behaviour predates this fix.
Behaviour predates this fix: registering by hand via PATCH does not regenerate the accounting entry, so it keeps the receipt date (16/11) instead of data_registrazione (05/02).

action_items: Optional: renumber or keep the original numero when rigenera regenerates an entry, so the libro giornale stays in date order.
Optional: in rigenera, skip invoices dated in the future (or report them in errori) instead of using a registration date earlier than the invoice date.
Optional: skip the accounting entry for contestata invoices.
critical_code_review_comments: rigenera marks the invoice 'registrata' before calling check_annullabile. If the existing entry is in a closed year, the HTTPException is swallowed: the invoice is registered but keeps the old entry with no error reported. The manual /registrazione endpoint checks first.
dr = min(max(data, YYYY-01-01), oggi): the max() does nothing. Only the cap at today matters, and it can give dr < data for future-dated invoices.
Ratei/risconti are not considered in the auto registration (acceptable, but different from the manual flow).
seed_data_creation: TEST_T89 company, user and session plus their documents were created and then fully cleaned up (verified 0 left).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: pytest tests/test_iteration89_rigenera_passive.py -n 0 (T89_KEEP=1 keeps the company for UI work). For UI: set cookie session_token=test_session_t89_admin and localStorage fe_company_id, and override window.confirm through page.evaluate, because the Playwright dialog handler has to be async.
